stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-prop.det.ch.justification: Both declarations add the mathematically contentful binder `[inst : CommRing R]`, whereas the blueprint only says “Let A ∈ K^{n×n}” and “Let x ∈ K” and nowhere assumes that K is a commutative ring. This is not merely an encoding instance: `CommRing` imposes algebraic laws, and `Matrix.det` itself has the required binder `[CommRing R]`. Thus the formal statements apply only after an additional hypothesis absent from the blueprint. Apart from this, the two declarations accurately represent the two displayed sums: `∑ P, … * x ^ (n - P.card)` ranges over all subsets of `Fin n`, while `k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1)` and `P.card = n - k` encode the grouped sum for `0 ≤ k ≤ n`; the ordered embeddings correctly form the principal submatrices. To make the package faithful, the blueprint would need to state that K is a commutative ring. If the literal unrestricted K is intended, the determinant dependency and theorem binders would instead have to be replaced by definitions under precisely the weaker algebraic structure intended.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-prop.det.x-.justification: The formal theorem quantifies `∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] ...`, and `constPlusDiagMatrix` likewise requires `[CommRing R]`. The blueprint only says “`d_1,…,d_n ∈ K` and `x ∈ K`” and never states that `K` is a commutative ring (or a field); none of its definition sections supplies such a setting. `CommRing` is mathematically contentful here, not merely an encoding requirement: commutativity is relevant to the displayed identity (already for `n = 2`, expanding the determinant involves `d₁x`, while the stated right side uses `xd₁`). Apart from this added binder, the matrix and formula agree: the dependency defines entries as `x + if i = j then d i else 0`, and the conclusion is the full product plus `x` times the sum of products omitting each index. To make the formalization faithful, the blueprint must explicitly assume that `K` is a commutative ring (or a field, in which case the Lean theorem is more general); alternatively, the target and `constPlusDiagMatrix` would need suitably weakened algebraic binders together with whatever centrality assumptions make the identity valid.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.pier.justification: Both declarations match the two Pieri rules. Their binders `∀ {N : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (mu : SymmetricFunctions.NPartition N)` formalize “Let n ∈ ℕ. Let μ be an N-partition” in the polynomial ring over a commutative coefficient ring. The horizontal conclusion uses `MvPolynomial.hsymm ... n * schur mu` and sums over `horizontalNStripPartitions mu n`; that dependency enforces containment through `potentialHorizontalStrips`, the condition `μ_i ≥ λ_{i+1}` through `isHorizontalStripFun`, and `|λ| = |μ| + n` through `hasSizeDiff`, exactly matching “λ/μ is a horizontal n-strip.” Likewise, `verticalNStripPartitions mu n` enforces containment, `λ_i ≤ μ_i + 1` via `isVerticalStripFun`, and the same size condition, exactly matching “vertical n-strip.” Finally, `schur` is the stated sum of tableau monomials, while the base-library meanings of `hsymm` and `esymm` are respectively the sums of all degree-`n` monomials and degree-`n` squarefree monomials. Quantification over every commutative ring is at least as general as the coefficient-ring setting of the blueprint and does not weaken either rule.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.schu.justification: The target quantifies over exactly the data of an N-partition: `lam : Fin N → ℕ` together with `hlam : ∀ (i j : Fin N), i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i`, matching “a weakly decreasing N-tuple of nonnegative integers.” Its conclusion `(SymmetricFunctions.schur { parts := lam, weaklyDecreasing := hlam }).IsSymmetric` matches “for any partition λ, s_λ is a symmetric polynomial.” The dependency `schur` is definitionally `∑ T ∈ ssytFinset lam, T.toMonomial`, matching `s_λ := ∑_{T ∈ SSYT(λ)} x_T`; the supplied SSYT and monomial definitions encode entries in `[N]`, row-weakness, column-strictness, and the product of corresponding variables. Finally, `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric` means invariance under all permutations of variables, exactly the informal definition of symmetric. The binder `[CommRing R]` supplies the coefficient-ring setting required by the formal polynomial and Schur definitions and agrees with the informal use of the polynomial ring `K[x₁,…,x_N]`; it is not an unrelated mathematical restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-cor.lgv.bin.justification: The formal binders `∀ {k : ℕ} (a b : Fin k → ℕ)` exactly encode a length-`k` pair of sequences of nonnegative integers. The hypotheses `(∀ (i j : Fin k), i ≤ j → a j ≤ a i)` and the analogous hypothesis for `b` express precisely the blueprint’s weakly decreasing conditions `a₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_k` and `b₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ b_k`; replacing indices `1,…,k` by the canonically ordered `Fin k` is only an indexing shift. The matrix entry `↑((a i).choose (b j))` is the integer cast of the natural binomial coefficient, agreeing with the informal binomial definition for nonnegative integer arguments. Finally, `Matrix.det` is the Leibniz determinant and the conclusion `0 ≤ ...det` states exactly that this integer determinant is nonnegative. The case `k = 0` is included on both sides since the blueprint quantifies over `k ∈ ℕ`.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-cor.lgv.cat.justification: The visible indexing and quantification align: the target quantifies `∀ (k : ℕ)`, and `LGV.catalanHankelMatrix` has entries `↑(catalan (↑i + ↑j))` for `i j : Fin k`, which is the zero-based counterpart of the blueprint’s `c_{i+j-2}` for `1 ≤ i,j ≤ k`. `Matrix.det` is also the Leibniz determinant required by the informal definition. However, the package gives no BASE-LIBRARY REF for the constant `catalan`. Thus it does not establish that the `catalan` used in the dependency body equals the blueprint sequence `c_n = 1/(n+1) * binom(2n,n)`. The dependency docstring calls it Catalan but does not define the imported constant. A signature and defining body or authoritative docstring for Mathlib’s `catalan` is needed to decide faithfulness.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-prop.fps.su.justification: The hypothesis “If `(f_i)_{i ∈ I}` is multipliable” is represented coefficientwise by `∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ M, ∀ (J : Finset I), M ⊆ J → coeff n (∏ i ∈ J, f i) = coeff n (∏ i ∈ M, f i)`, exactly expressing that every coefficient stabilizes after a finite determining subset. The condition `PowerSeries.constantCoeff g = 0` matches `[x^0]g = 0`. The conclusion repeats the same multipliability condition for `PowerSeries.subst g (f i)`, which is the formal substitution corresponding to `f_i ∘ g = f_i[g]`. The binders `{K} [CommRing K]` and `{I}` match the stated setting. `[DecidableEq I]` is an implementation-level instance needed for finite-set products, not a mathematically substantive restriction on the index family.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.det.det.justification: The formal declaration adds the mathematically substantive binder `∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R]`, whereas the blueprint only says that `A` and `D` are matrices in `K^{n×n}` and nowhere declares that `K` is a commutative ring. The supplied informal determinant definition uses operations in `K` but does not state axioms fixing this setting, and the instructions prohibit assuming an omitted ambient field or ring convention. This restriction also enters through `Matrix.det`, whose signature requires `[CommRing R]`. The remainder matches: `Matrix.diagonal d` represents a diagonal `D`, the sum ranges over all finsets `P ⊆ Fin n`, `orderEmbOfFin` forms the increasing principal submatrix, and `Pᶜ` gives the complementary diagonal product. To make the statement faithful, the blueprint must explicitly specify that `K` is a commutative ring (or a stronger setting such as a field, in which case the Lean theorem is more general); alternatively, the formal determinant infrastructure and theorem would need to use whatever algebraic setting the blueprint actually intends.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-e.justification: The target adds and narrows mathematically substantive hypotheses absent from the blueprint. First, it requires `∀ (hcontained : ∀ (i : Fin N), mu i ≤ lam i), ...`, while the informal statement merely says “Let λ and μ be two partitions” and the informal definitions explicitly define `s_{λ/μ}` even without containment (there are then no tableaux). This restriction enters through both the target binder `hcontained` and the dependency `SkewPartition.mk ... → inner ≤ outer → SkewPartition N`, since project `skewSchur` only accepts a bundled contained skew partition. Faithfulness would require defining `skewSchur` for arbitrary pairs of partitions, with the non-contained case represented by the empty tableau sum, and removing `hcontained` from the theorem (or an equivalent case-based formulation). Second, the blueprint has an independent determinant size `M`: “Let M ∈ ℕ be such that both λᵗ and μᵗ have length ≤ M,” whereas the target uses one index `N` everywhere: `lam mu lamt muT : Fin N → ℕ`, `MvPolynomial.esymm (Fin N)`, and a determinant indexed by `Fin N`. Thus it forces the number of rows/variables and the padded transpose length/determinant size to coincide, and `IsTranspose lam lamt` with both tuples indexed by `Fin N` additionally forces the diagram to fit in an `N × N` box. The available `IsTranspose` declaration already supports distinct lengths `{N M}`, so the theorem should instead quantify separate `N` and `M`, take `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ`, `lamt muT : Fin M → ℕ`, use `IsTranspose lam lamt`, and form a `Fin M × Fin M` determinant whose entries are `esymm (Fin N) R ...`.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.jt-h.justification: The target exactly formalizes the non-skew Jacobi–Trudi identity. Its binders `(lam : Fin N → ℕ) (hlam : ∀ (i j : Fin N), i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i)` encode an `N`-partition, matching “For non-skew Schur polynomials” and the informal use of `λ`. The left side is `SymmetricFunctions.schur { parts := lam, weaklyDecreasing := hlam }`, whose body is the stipulated tableau sum `∑ T ∈ ssytFinset lam, T.toMonomial`, matching `s_λ := ∑_{T∈SSYT(λ)} x_T`. On the right, `(SymmetricFunctions.jacobiTrudiMatrixH lam fun x => 0).det` specializes the skew matrix to `μ = 0`. By the matrix definition, entry `(i,j)` is `hsymmExt (↑(lam i) - 0 - ↑i + ↑j)`, hence `h_{λ_i-i+j}`. Although `Fin N` uses zero-based indices while the displayed formula uses `1 ≤ i,j ≤ N`, shifting both indices by one leaves `-i+j` unchanged. Finally, `hsymmExt` supplies the required convention `h_n=0` for negative `n` and `h_0=1`. The arbitrary `[CommRing R]` is the coefficient-ring setting required by the project’s Schur-polynomial and determinant definitions, not an extra restriction on partitions or indices.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.lr-z.justification:
The elaborated signature adds the mathematically contentful binder `[IsDomain R]` on top of `[CommRing R]`: `∀ {R} [CommRing R] ... [IsDomain R] ...`. The blueprint merely states the polynomial identity and its definition of `𝒫` only says “the polynomial ring K[x₁,…,x_N]”; it does not require K to be a domain. Since the project’s `schurPoly` and `skewSchurPoly` are already defined for every `CommRing R`, this restriction is not needed merely to encode the statement. Removing `[IsDomain R]` would fix this drift (and would give a more general, hence faithful, theorem).

There is also a dependency-level mismatch for non-contained shapes. The blueprint explicitly says: “If we don’t have μ ⊆ λ, then we agree that there are no Young tableaux of shape λ/μ.” But `AlgebraicCombinatorics.Tableau` is unconditionally defined as `{ c // c ∈ skewYoungDiagram lam mu } → Fin N`, with `skewYoungDiagram lam mu = {c | mu c.1 < c.2 ∧ c.2 ≤ lam c.1}`. Thus, when `μ ⊄ λ`, the formal tableau type need not be empty—it may retain cells from rows where `μ_i < λ_i`—and consequently both `skewSchurPoly` and the Yamanouchi-indexed sum can denote different objects from the blueprint. Because the theorem quantifies over all three N-partitions without assuming `μ ⊆ λ`, this matters. To match the blueprint without narrowing the theorem, the `Tableau`/skew-tableau dependency (and consequently the associated sums) should be defined to have no tableaux when `μ ⊄ λ`; merely adding `μ ⊆ λ` to the target would itself narrow the blueprint statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-thm.sf.skew.justification: The blueprint says: “for any partitions λ ⊇ μ, s_{λ/μ} is a symmetric polynomial.” The formal binders exactly encode two N-partitions and containment: `lam mu : Fin N → ℕ`, `hlam` and `hmu` require weak decrease, and `hcontained : ∀ i, mu i ≤ lam i` matches `μ ⊆ λ`. The conclusion `(SymmetricFunctions.skewSchur ...).IsSymmetric` uses `skewSchur`, whose body is the sum of `T.toMonomial` over all skew SSYTs, and `MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric`, meaning invariance under permutations of variables, matching the informal definitions. The binder `[CommRing R]` is the coefficient-ring setting required by the project’s polynomial and skew-Schur definitions, not an unrelated added hypothesis. Quantification over arbitrary `N` and arbitrary commutative coefficient ring is at least as general as the blueprint’s fixed `N` and `K`. The Jacobi–Trudi wording describes the proof route rather than adding a separate mathematical conclusion to the theorem statement.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-cor.lgv.kpa.justification: The formal hypotheses correctly encode the four weak coordinate chains: `LGV.xDecreasing A → LGV.yIncreasing A → LGV.xDecreasing B → LGV.yIncreasing B →`, and the formal conclusion correctly matches the final displayed identity. In particular, `LGV.nipatWeightSum ... A B (Equiv.refl (Fin k))` unfolds to the sum of weights of non-intersecting path tuples from `A` to `B`; the unused permutation argument causes no mismatch at the identity. However, the blueprint also explicitly concludes: “there are no nipats from A to σ(B) when σ ∈ S_k is not the identity permutation.” The target conclusion contains only the determinant equality and has no binder `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)`, no hypothesis `σ ≠ Equiv.refl (Fin k)`, and no emptiness/nonexistence assertion for nipats from `A` to the permuted `B`. Thus it formalizes only the stated consequence, not the full blueprint claim. To make it faithful, the target should additionally conclude, for every nonidentity `σ`, that `LGV.nipatSet A (fun i => B (σ i))` is empty (or equivalently that no such `PathTuple` is non-intersecting), together with the determinant equality.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-cor.pars.pn.justification: The binder `∀ n > 0` exactly matches “For each positive integer n.” The dependency `partitionCount n := Fintype.card n.Partition` matches the defined partition number `p(n)`, and `pentagonalNumber k := ((3 * k - 1) * k / 2).toNat` represents the defined nonnegative integer `w_k = ((3k-1)k)/2`. The formal coefficient `if (↑k).natAbs % 2 = 1 then 1 else -1` has the same parity pattern as `(-1)^(k-1)`: it is positive for odd k and negative for even k, including negative k since absolute value preserves parity. The formal sum restricts to `k ≠ 0 ∧ pentagonalNumber k ≤ n`, whereas the blueprint writes all `k ∈ ℤ`, `k ≠ 0`; this is not a substantive narrowing because when `w_k > n`, the integer `n-w_k` is negative and there are no partitions of it, so the omitted terms are zero. Under the restriction, the formal natural subtraction `n - pentagonalNumber k` agrees with integer subtraction. Enumerating the surviving indices as `1,-1,2,-2,…` yields the displayed terms at offsets `1,2,5,7,12,15,22,26,…`, so the explicit expansion is the same sum rewritten.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.fps.inf.justification: The formal hypothesis `PowerSeries.constantCoeff g = 0` exactly represents `[x^0]g = 0`. Its approximator hypothesis, `∀ k ≤ n, ∀ (J : Finset I), M ⊆ J → coeff k (∏ i ∈ J, f i) = coeff k (∏ i ∈ M, f i)`, matches “for all `k ≤ n` and `J ⊇ M`” in the definition of an `x^n`-approximator. The conclusion likewise quantifies over every finite `J : Finset I` containing `M` and equates the `n`th coefficients of the corresponding products after substitution; `PowerSeries.subst g (f i)` represents substituting `g` into `f i`, i.e. `f_i ∘ g`. The binders `[CommRing K]` provide the algebraic setting required by the FPS products and substitution, while `[DecidableEq I]` is an implementation requirement for finite sets rather than a mathematically contentful restriction.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.jtp.par.justification: The target states exactly `partitionGenFun * pentagonalSeries = 1` in `PowerSeries ℤ`, matching “We have P·Q = 1.” The body `PowerSeries.mk fun n => ↑(partitionCount n)` agrees with `P = ∑_{n≥0} p(n)x^n`, since `partitionCount n = Fintype.card n.Partition`. Likewise, `pentagonalSeries` has coefficient `↑(pentagonalCoeff n)`, where `pentagonalCoeff` returns `(-1) ^ k.natAbs` when the inverse finds `n = w_k` and `0` otherwise, matching the blueprint’s explicitly defined coefficient `(-1)^{|k|}`. Finally, `pentagonalNumber k = ((3*k - 1)*k/2).toNat` represents the specified nonnegative integer `w_k = ((3k-1)k)/2`. There are no added hypotheses or narrowed quantifiers in the elaborated target.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.schu.justification: The target quantifies over `lam : Fin N → ℕ` and assumes `AlgebraicCombinatorics.IsNPartition lam`, whose body is `∀ i j, i ≤ j → lam j ≤ lam i`; this exactly represents the blueprint’s “Let λ be an N-partition,” i.e. a weakly decreasing N-tuple of naturals. Its conclusion `alternant (lam + rho N) = alternant (rho N) * schurPoly lam` directly matches `a_{λ+ρ} = a_ρ · s_λ`. Here `rho N i = N - 1 - ↑i` is `(N-1,…,0)`, and function addition is componentwise tuple addition. The formal `alternant` expands as the signed permutation sum with exponent tuple `α ∘ σ`, which is the determinant expansion of `(x_i^{α_j})`. Finally, `schurPoly lam = skewSchurPoly lam 0` expands to the sum of content monomials over semistandard tableaux of shape `λ/0`, matching the informal tableau definition of `s_λ`. Quantification over every commutative coefficient ring `R` is compatible with, and potentially more general than, the blueprint’s polynomial ring setting; it does not weaken the claimed relation.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-prop.fps.su.justification: The blueprint quantifies over an arbitrary FPS “$g\in K[[x]]$ … satisfying $[x^0]g=0$” and asserts both that “$(f_i\circ g)_{i\in I}$ is multipliable” and the product identity. The target instead binds only “$(a : K)$” and uses `PowerSeries.rescale a`, whose docstring says it substitutes only `aX`; thus it covers the special case $g=aX$, and its conclusion contains only the equality, not multipliability of the substituted family. More fundamentally, the supplied formal vocabulary contains no operation for composition by an arbitrary zero-constant power series and no coefficient-finite-determination predicate. The target’s `Multipliable f` is the base-library topological notion that `f` has an unconditional infinite product, whereas the informal definition requires every coefficient to be finitely determined. The added binders `[TopologicalSpace K] [IsTopologicalRing K] [T2Space K]` enter through this different `Multipliable`/`tprod` formulation and are not part of the blueprint definition. To make the statement faithful, the project would need definitions of arbitrary FPS composition, zero constant coefficient, and the blueprint’s coefficientwise multipliability/product; the theorem should then quantify over `g : PowerSeries K`, assume its constant coefficient is zero, conclude `Multipliable (fun i => compose (f i) g)`, and state the corresponding product identity.
